items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: Vytavec used to come out with me. I used to get five dollars a night, so we'd buy a couple of pints of gin. Vytavec would come out... I stuck up with friendships... Vytavec, and I would sit in as a cornet team.

ctx.x: I was sick. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I wasn't working with the New Orleans Rhythm Kings, I was working on Clark Street. And I'd be down to New Orleans Rhythm Kings, Mike Frenzel, if they'd get off early, we'd go out to where Joe was working and sit around and listen. And by the fact, we started out originally as a cornet team. Oh, would you talk about that a little? I didn't know that. Well, sure. I was working at the Vista dance hall on 43rd Street three nights a week. Vytavec used to come out with me. I used to get…

He was working in Chicago on Charlie Strait. This was the winter of 22. He had a Peewee with him, a drum boy. He had a band at the Arcade in St. Louis on the Alice Street. Well, he was around 22. He was in Chicago. The winter of 22. No, he was in Chicago then.
